name: Oscar Scherer State Park
evidence: Reserve Florida per-site data (rdr/fd/units, 2026-10-26): RV sites 1-17 and 70-90 'adjacent to a creek' (South Creek), 15-36 ft; their GIS points on Esri imagery sit ~20-35 m from the creek under bank canopy (no road or used strip between). Lake Osprey is not the water here.

name: Rainbow Springs State Park Campground
evidence: Reserve Florida per-site GIS points (all campsites 29.0862-29.0899, -82.4227 to -82.4207) plotted on Esri at 29.0879,-82.4221: every site ~280 m+ from the Rainbow River through continuous forest; no site description mentions the river

name: Sportsman's Cove Resort
evidence: Esri 215 m frame at 29.4502,-82.2133: a row of occupied RV sites on open grass ~5-10 m from the resort's boat canal, which opens ~150 m E into Orange Lake (pond by the boat basin too); operator sells 'Waterside' RV sites (rates.htm). Same call as 14625's canal to Cass Lake

name: Wickham Park Campground
evidence: Esri 140 m frames at 28.1660,-80.6650 and 28.1648,-80.6648: RV pads ~15-25 m from two campground ponds across open grass with scattered trees, which bears out AWH's firsthand 'several sites are on small ponds'. The county saying no 'water access/view' sites is about how it prices sites

name: RV Village at Lake Panasoffkee
evidence: operator site map (site-map-060723) + Esri 120 m frame at 28.7598,-82.1075: the water (Outlet River at the lake) is met only by the ramp, boathouse, fishing pier and sleeping cabins; the nearest RV pads (premium L sites) are ~50 m back behind that used cabin/ramp strip and trees

name: Ocean Pond Campground (Osceola National Forest)
evidence: rec.gov per-site coords (search API, no Proximity to Water flags) on Esri: the nearest Water-loop pads (31, 33, 40, 42, 44) are ~15-35 m behind a continuous cypress/shrub-wetland fringe, then 20-40 m of emergent marsh before open water. 'Lakeside access' in the prose is not counting evidence

name: Pine Lake RV Park
evidence: Esri 230 m frame at 30.5287,-85.3942: Pine Lake (a narrow pond) lies S/SE of the RV rows, ~55-65 m from the nearest RV behind trees and the clubhouse. A cleared strip along its west bank (posts, no RVs) has a tree band to the water. The operator's 'along the shimmering waters' is marketing

name: St. Petersburg / Madeira Beach KOA Holiday
evidence: Esri 100-160 m frames at 27.8212,-82.7698 and 27.8228,-82.7704: rebuilt shore-side patio pads sit ~10-25 m from Long Bayou behind a continuous mangrove belt (silt fence, kayak cuts and a dock). The open lawn to the water is an activity area; the pond is ringed by park models. A 'Kayak Access' site-type name can't upgrade
